paragraphs.sourceText: Listen to the following passage. Altogether the passage will be read to you four times. During the first reading, which will be done at normal speed, listen and try to understand the meaning. For the second and third readings, the passage, except the first sentence, will be read sentence by sentence, or phrase by phrase, with intervals of 15 seconds. The last reading will be done at normal speed again and during this time you should check your work. You will then be given ONE minute to check your work once more.
paragraphs.translationZh: 听下面这段话。这篇文章总共会读给你四遍。在第一次阅读时，将以正常速度完成，聆听并尝试理解其含义。第二、三读时，除第一句外，逐句或逐词朗读，间隔15秒。最后一次阅读将再次以正常速度完成，在此期间您应该检查您的工作。然后您将有一分钟的时间再次检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: Write on ANSWER SHEET ONE. The first sentence of the passage is already provided.
paragraphs.translationZh: 写在第一张答题纸上。该段落的第一句话已经提供。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，请听这段话。

paragraphs.sourceText: China’s Parcel Delivery Business
paragraphs.translationZh: 中国包裹递送业务

paragraphs.sourceText: China’s parcel delivery business has boomed in the past decade.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去十年，中国的包裹递送业务蓬勃发展。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear a talk. You will hear the talk ONCE ONLY. While listening, you may look at the task on ANSWER SHEET ONE and write NO MORE THAN THREE WORDS for each gap. Make sure what you fill in is both grammatically and semantically acceptable. You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到一场演讲。您只会听到一次演讲。听力时，您可以查看第一张答题卡上的任务，并为每个空白写不超过三个单词。确保您填写的内容在语法和语义上都是可接受的。您可以使用空白纸做笔记。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览填补空白的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now listen to the talk. When it is over, you will be given TWO minutes to check your work.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在听一下演讲。结束后，您将有两分钟时间检查您的工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section you will hear two conversations. At the end of each conversation, five questions will be asked about what was said. Both the conversations and the questions will be spoken ONCE ONLY. After each question there will be a ten-second pause. During the pause, you should read the four choices of A, B, C and D, and mark the best answer to each question on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在本节中，您将听到两个对话。每次对话结束时，都会针对谈话内容提出五个问题。对话和问题都只会说一次。每个问题后都会有十秒钟的停顿。暂停期间，您应该阅读 A、B、C、D 四个选项，并在第二张答题卡上标记每个问题的最佳答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: You have THIRTY seconds to preview the choices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您有三十秒的时间来预览选项。

paragraphs.sourceText: Now, listen to the conversations.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现在，听听对话。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 1 to 5 are based on Conversation One.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 1 至 5 基于对话一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 6 to 10 are based on Conversation Two.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 6 至 10 基于对话二。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are twenty sentences in this section. Beneath each sentence there are four options marked A, B, C and D.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节共有二十句话。每个句子下面有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。

paragraphs.sourceText: Choose the one that best completes the sentence or answers the question. Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 选择最能完成句子或回答问题的一项。在第二张答题卡上标记您的答案。

paragraphs.sourceText: 11. Awaiting me is a demanding job that I just don’t know ________ I’m going to do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 11. 等待着我的是一项艰巨的工作，我只是不知道________我要做什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: 12. By the end of last month, our cute baby ________ in this world for 100 days.
paragraphs.translationZh: 12. 上个月底，我们可爱的宝宝________在这个世界上已经100天了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 13. ________ wounded soldier was ________ good old friend of his.
14. The children were ________ hungry and each of them could have eaten a horse.
paragraphs.translationZh: 14. 孩子们________ 饿了，每个人都可以吃掉一匹马。

paragraphs.sourceText: 15. ________ your generous assistance, I couldn’t have accomplished this daunting task in time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 15. ________ 您的慷慨帮助，我无法及时完成这项艰巨的任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 16. She was impressed by the view of ________ mountains behind the apple orchard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 16. 苹果园后面的________山脉的景色给她留下了深刻的印象。

paragraphs.sourceText: 17. In phrases like biting cold, scorching hot, or dazzling bright, the -ING participle is used as ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 17. 在像 Biting Cold、Scorching Hot 或 dazzling Bright 这样的短语中，-ING 分词用作 ________。

paragraphs.translationZh: 18.“街角曾经有一个公共汽车站。”句子中斜体部分表示

paragraphs.translationZh: 19.“本来我们现在就到了，但是堵车太严重了。”斜体部分表示________。

paragraphs.sourceText: 20. “Alice has an urgent task, and she must be working late at the office now.” The italicized word in the sentence expresses ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 20.“爱丽丝有一项紧急任务，她现在肯定在办公室工作到很晚。”句子中的斜体字表示________。

paragraphs.sourceText: 21. He tricked the kid ________ trusting him by pretending that he had super power.
paragraphs.translationZh: 21. 他假装拥有超能力，欺骗了孩子________信任他。

paragraphs.sourceText: 22. Everyone in the company agrees that their boss is a very resourceful and ________ man.
paragraphs.translationZh: 22. 公司里的每个人都同意他们的老板是一个非常足智多谋且________的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 23. In ________ of the strong earthquake last week, many families are deep in mourning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 23. 在上周发生的强烈地震________中，许多家庭都沉浸在悲痛之中。

paragraphs.sourceText: 24. The factory is looking for better ways to ________ operations so as to improve productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 24. 工厂正在寻找更好的方法来进行________操作，以提高生产率。

paragraphs.sourceText: 25. The unique wall paintings in the old town are once again under the media ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 25. 老城区独特的壁画再次被媒体报道________。

paragraphs.sourceText: 26. Please excuse me. I must ________ to some urgent business now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 26.请原谅。我现在必须________处理一些紧急事务。

paragraphs.translationZh: 27. Tim 一点也不成熟，很容易失去他的________，这有时可能会伤害他周围的人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 28. She often let the children play in the yard to keep them out of ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 28. 她经常让孩子们在院子里玩耍，以免他们受到________的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: 29. The overall economic ________ for the newly emerging economy is very promising.
paragraphs.translationZh: 29. 新兴经济体的整体经济________是非常有前途的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 30. They normally ________ one of their three arguments when criticizing their opponents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 30. 当批评他们的对手时，他们通常会________他们的三个论点之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: Decide which of the words given in the box below would best complete the passage if inserted in the corresponding
blank. The words can be used ONCE ONLY. Mark the letter for each word on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 空白。这些词只能使用一次。在答题纸二上标记每个单词的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Tiny is mighty, at least when it comes to change. Over the last twenty years, I’ve found that almost everyone wants to make some kind of change: lose weight, get better sleep, reduce stress. We want to be more productive and creative. But the alarming levels of (31) ________, sleeplessness, and stress reported by the media tell me there is a painful (32)________ between what people want and what they actually do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 微小就是强大，至少在改变方面是这样。在过去的二十年里，我发现几乎每个人都想做出某种改变：减肥、改善睡眠、减轻压力。我们希望变得更有生产力和创造力。但媒体报道的肥胖、失眠和压力的惊人水平告诉我，人们想要的和他们实际做的之间存在着令人痛苦的差距。

paragraphs.sourceText: The disconnection between want and do has been blamed on a lot of things — but people blame it on (33) ________ for the most part. When our results fall (34) ________ of our expectations, many of us believe that something must be wrong with us. If (35) ________ we were better people, we wouldn’t have failed. Right?
paragraphs.translationZh: 想要和做之间的脱节被归咎于很多事情——但人们在很大程度上将其归咎于自己。当我们的结果没有达到我们的预期时，我们中的许多人都认为我们一定出了什么问题。如果我们是更好的人，我们就不会失败。正确的？

paragraphs.sourceText: NO. It isn’t your fault, and creating positive change isn’t as hard as you think. For too many years, myths, misconceptions, and well-meaning but unscientific advice have (36) ________ you up to fail. If you’ve attempted change in the past and haven’t seen results, you may have concluded that change is hard or that you can’t succeed because you (37) ________ motivation. Neither is accurate. The problem is with the approach itself, not with you.
paragraphs.translationZh: 没有。这不是你的错，创造积极的改变并不像你想象的那么难。多年来，神话、误解和善意但不科学的建议都让你走向失败。如果您过去尝试过改变但没有看到结果，您可能会得出这样的结论：改变很困难，或者因为缺乏动力而无法成功。两者都不准确。问题出在方法本身，而不是你。

paragraphs.sourceText: Building (38) ________ and creating positive changes can be easy — if you have the right approach. In order to design successful habits and change your behaviors, the following three methods should be adopted in the very beginning. First, stop judging yourself. Second, take your aspirations and break them down into (39) ________ behaviors. Third, embrace mistakes as discoveries and use them to move (40) ________.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果你有正确的方法，养成习惯和创造积极的改变可以很容易。为了设计成功的习惯并改变你的行为，一开始就应该采用以下三种方法。首先，停止评判自己。其次，把你的愿望分解成微小的行为。第三，将错误视为发现并利用它们前进。

paragraphs.sourceText: In this section there are three passages followed by ten multiple choice questions. For each multiple choice question, there are four suggested answers marked A, B, C and D. Choose the one that you think is the best answer and mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET TWO.
paragraphs.translationZh: 本节由三篇文章组成，后面是十个多项选择题。对于每个多项选择题，有四个建议答案，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。选择您认为最佳答案的一个，并将您的答案标记在答题表二上。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) Downturn’s new spending habits show the way to greater satisfaction.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 经济低迷时期的新消费习惯指明了提高满意度的途径。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) As the months passed, out went stacks of sweaters, shoes, pots and pans, even the television after a trial separation during which it was relegated to a closet. Eventually, Tammy Strobel and her husband Logan Smith, both 31, got rid of their cars, too. Her mother called her crazy. Today, three years after the couple began downsizing, they live in a studio with a nice-sized kitchen. They have money to travel and to contribute to the education funds of nieces and nephews. Because their debt is paid off, Ms. Strobel works fewer hours, giving her time to be outdoors and to volunteer. “The idea that you need to go bigger to be happy is false,” she says. “I really believe that the acquisition of material goods doesn’t bring about happiness.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 几个月过去了，成堆的毛衣、鞋子、锅碗瓢盆都被扔掉了，甚至电视在尝试分离后也被收进了壁橱。最终，塔米·斯特罗贝尔 (Tammy Strobel) 和她 31 岁的丈夫洛根·史密斯 (Logan Smith) 也扔掉了他们的汽车。她的母亲称她疯了。如今，在这对夫妇开始缩小规模三年后，他们住在一间带宽敞厨房的单间公寓里。他们有钱去旅行，并为侄子侄女的教育基金捐款。由于债务已还清，史特博女士的工作时间减少了，这让她有时间在户外活动和做志愿者。 “你需要变得更大才能快乐的想法是错误的，”她说。 “我真的相信，获得物质财富并不能带来幸福。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) While Ms. Strobel and her husband overhauled their spending habits before the recession, legions of other consumers have since had to adapt in ways that could ultimately make them happier.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 虽然史特博女士和她的丈夫在经济衰退前彻底改变了他们的消费习惯，但此后大批其他消费者不得不以最终让他们更快乐的方式进行调整。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) New studies of consumption and happiness show, for instance, that people are happier when they spend money on experiences instead of material objects.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 例如，关于消费和幸福的新研究表明，当人们把钱花在体验而不是物质上时，他们会更幸福。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) While the current round of stinginess may simply be a response to the economic downturn, some analysts say consumers may also be permanently adjusting their spending based on what they’ve discovered about what truly makes them happy or fulfilled.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 虽然当前这一轮的吝啬可能只是对经济衰退的反应，但一些分析师表示，消费者也可能会根据他们发现的真正让他们快乐或满足的东西来永久调整他们的支出。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) “This actually is a topic that hasn’t been researched very much until recently,” says Elizabeth Dunn, a psychology professor, who is at the forefront of research on consumption and happiness. “There’s massive literature on income and happiness. It’s amazing how little there is on how to spend your money.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) “这实际上是一个直到最近才得到广泛研究的话题，”心理学教授伊丽莎白·邓恩 (Elizabeth Dunn) 说，她处于消费与幸福研究的前沿。 “有大量关于收入和幸福的文献。令人惊讶的是，关于如何花钱的文献却很少。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) Studies over the last few decades have shown that money, up to a certain point, makes people happier because it lets them meet basic needs. The latest round of research is all about emotional efficiency: how to reap the most happiness for your dollar.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 过去几十年的研究表明，金钱在某种程度上可以使人们更快乐，因为它可以让他们满足基本需求。最新一轮的研究都是关于情感效率的：如何用你的钱获得最大的幸福。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) One major finding is that spending money for an experience — concert tickets, language lessons, dumpling-making classes — produces longer-lasting satisfaction than spending money on plain old stuff. “‘It’s better to go on a vacation than buy a new couch’ is basically the idea,” says Professor Dunn. Jennifer Black, president of the retailing research company Jennifer Black & Associates, said: “I think people are realizing they don’t need what they had. They’re more interested in creating memories.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 一个重要的发现是，花钱获得体验——音乐会门票、语言课程、包饺子课程——比花钱买普通的旧东西能产生更持久的满足感。 “‘去度假比买新沙发更好’基本上是这个想法，”邓恩教授说。零售研究公司 Jennifer Black & Associates 总裁 Jennifer Black 表示：“我认为人们正在意识到他们不需要他们拥有的东西。他们更感兴趣的是创造回忆。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) Unlike consumption of material goods, spending on leisure and services typically strengthens social bonds, which in turn helps amplify happiness, research suggests. Paying for experiences also gives us longer-lasting happiness, because we can reminisce about them, researchers says. That’s true for even the most exasperating of experiences. That trip to Rome during which you waited in endless lines, broke your camera and argued with your spouse will typically be airbrushed with “rosy recollection”, says Professor Dunn. “Trips aren’t all perfect, but we remember them as perfect.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) 研究表明，与物质商品消费不同，休闲和服务支出通常会加强社会纽带，从而有助于增强幸福感。研究人员表示，为体验付费还可以给我们带来更持久的快乐，因为我们可以回忆起它们。即使是最令人恼火的经历也是如此。邓恩教授说，那次罗马之行，你排着长队等待，弄坏了相机，还与配偶争吵，这些经历通常都会被抹上“美好的回忆”。 “旅行并不都是完美的，但我们记得它们是完美的。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (10) And experiences can’t be absorbed at once — it takes more time to adapt to them and engage with them than it does to put on a new leather jacket or turn on that shiny flat-screen TV. “We buy a new house, we get accustomed to it,” says Professor Lyubomirsky, who studies what psychologists call “hedonic adaptation”, a phenomenon in which people quickly become used to changes, great or terrible, in order to maintain a stable level of happiness. “We stop getting pleasure from it,” she says. And then, of course, we buy new things. Scholars have discovered that one way consumers combat hedonic adaptation is to buy many small pleasures instead of one big one. Instead of a new Jaguar, Professor Lyubomirsky advises, buy a massage once a week, have lots of fresh flowers delivered and make phone calls to friends overseas. Instead of a two-week long vacation, take a few three-day weekends. “We do adapt to the little things,” she says, “but because there’s so many, it will take longer.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (10) 经验不可能一下子就被吸收——适应它们并与之互动需要比穿上新皮夹克或打开闪亮的平板电视更多的时间。 “我们买了一栋新房子，我们习惯了它，”柳博米尔斯基教授说，他研究心理学家所说的“享乐适应”，在这种现象中，人们很快就会习惯变化，无论是巨大的还是可怕的，以保持稳定的幸福水平。 “我们不再从中得到乐趣，”她说。然后，当然，我们会购买新东西。学者们发现，消费者对抗享乐适应的一种方式是购买许多小乐趣而不是一件大乐趣。柳博米尔斯基教授建议，不要买新的捷豹汽车，而是每周做一次按摩，送很多鲜花，给海外的朋友打电话。不要享受两周的长假，而是享受几个三天的周末。 “我们确实会适应小事情，”她说，“但因为事情太多，所以需要更长的时间。”

paragraphs.sourceText: (11) Ms. Strobel now writes about her own life choices on the Internet. “My lifestyle now would not be possible if I still had a huge two-bedroom apartment filled with stuff, two cars, and 30 grand in debt,” she says. “Give away some of your stuff. See how it feels.”
paragraphs.translationZh: (11) 史特博女士现在在互联网上写下她自己的人生选择。 “如果我仍然拥有一套装满东西的巨大两居室公寓、两辆车和 30 英镑的债务，我现在的生活方式将是不可能的，”她说。 “放弃你的一些东西。看看感觉如何。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. What is the main reason for the change in people’s spending habits?
paragraphs.translationZh: 41.人们消费习惯改变的主要原因是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Which of the following statements is TRUE according to the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 根据本文，以下哪项陈述是正确的？

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. What is the best title for the passage?
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 这篇文章的最佳标题是什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) The five o’clock dads can only be seen on cable television these days. They eat dinner with their television families and provide counsel afterward in the den, exemplifying how men behave when they work eight hours a day.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 如今，五点钟爸爸只能在有线电视上看到。他们与电视上的家人一起吃晚饭，然后在书房里提供建议，举例说明男人每天工作八小时时的行为方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) The five o’clock dad has become an endangered species. A corporate culture that believes presence is productivity, in which people of ambition are afraid to be seen leaving the office, has lengthened his workday and shortened his home life. So has an economy that makes it difficult for families to take a break even at the end of the month. For the man who is paid by the hour, that means never saying no to overtime. For the man whose loyalty to the organization is measured in time at his desk, it means goodbye to nine to five.
paragraphs.translationZh: （2）五点钟爸爸已经成为濒临灭绝的物种。相信存在就是生产力的企业文化，有抱负的人害怕被人看到离开办公室，这延长了他的工作时间，缩短了他的家庭生活。经济状况也是如此，家庭在月底很难实现收支平衡。对于按小时计酬的人来说，这意味着永远不要拒绝加班。对于那些对组织的忠诚度是以坐在办公桌前的时间来衡量的人来说，这意味着告别朝九晚五的日子。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) To lots of small children it means a visiting father. The standard joke in one large corporate office is that the dads always say their children look like angels when they’re sleeping because that’s the only way they ever see them. A survey taken several years ago showed that roughly 12 percent of the men surveyed with children under the age of six worked more than sixty hours a week, and an additional 25 percent worked between fifty and sixty hours.
paragraphs.translationZh: (3) 对于很多小孩子来说，这意味着来访的父亲。一家大型公司办公室里的标准笑话是，爸爸们总是说他们的孩子在睡觉时看起来像天使，因为这是他们看到孩子的唯一方式。几年前进行的一项调查显示，在接受调查的有六岁以下儿童的男性中，大约 12% 的男性每周工作时间超过 60 小时，另外 25% 的男性工作时间在 50 到 60 小时之间。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) No matter how you divide it up, those are twelve-hour days. When a talk show host adopted a baby recently, she said one reason she was not troubled by becoming a mother without becoming a wife was that many of her married female friends were “functionally single”, given the hours their husbands worked. The evening commuter rush is getting longer. The eight o’clock dad. The nine o’clock dad.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 不管你怎么划分，那都是十二小时的日子。一位脱口秀主持人最近收养了一个婴儿，她说，她不为成为母亲而不成为妻子而感到困扰的一个原因是，考虑到丈夫的工作时间，她的许多已婚女性朋友“实际上是单身”。晚上的通勤高峰时间越来越长。八点钟的爸爸。九点钟的爸爸。

paragraphs.sourceText: (5) There’s a horribly sad irony to this, that is, the quality of fathering is better than it was when the dads left work at five o’clock and came home to coffee pots and tuna casserole. The five o’clock dad was remote, a “wait till your father gets home” kind of dad with a newspaper for a face. The roles he and his wife had were clear: she did nurture and home, he did discipline and money.
paragraphs.translationZh: (5) 对此有一个极其悲伤的讽刺，那就是，父亲的质量比爸爸们五点钟下班回家喝着咖啡壶和金枪鱼砂锅的时候要好。五点钟的爸爸很遥远，是一个“等你爸爸回家”的爸爸，脸上一张报纸。他和妻子的角色很明确：她负责抚养和家庭，他负责管教和赚钱。

paragraphs.sourceText: (6) The role fathers have carved out for themselves today is a vast improvement, a muddling of those old boundaries. Fathers today do seem to be more emotional with their children, more nurturing, more open. Many say, “My father never told me he loved me” and so they tell their own children all the time that they love them.
paragraphs.translationZh: (6) 今天，父亲们为自己制定的角色是一个巨大的进步，是对那些旧界限的混乱。今天的父亲们似乎确实对孩子更加感性、更加有教养、更加开放。许多人说，“我的父亲从未告诉过我他爱我”，因此他们总是告诉自己的孩子他们爱他们。

paragraphs.sourceText: (7) There are people who think that this is changing even now. A nonprofit organization advises corporations on how to balance personal and professional obligations and concerns, and its founder says she has noticed a change in the past few years. An increasing number of men have expressed their wishes to spend more time with their kids.
paragraphs.translationZh: (7) 有些人认为这种情况现在正在改变。一个非营利组织就如何平衡个人和职业义务与担忧向企业提供建议，其创始人表示，她注意到过去几年发生了变化。越来越多的男性表示希望花更多时间陪伴孩子。

paragraphs.sourceText: (8) This change can be to the good, not only for women but especially for men, and for kids, too. The stereotypical five o’clock dad belongs in a picture, with his “Ask your mother” and his “Don’t be a crybaby.” The father who believes hugs and kisses are sex-blind and a dirty diaper requires a change is infinitely preferable. What a joy it would be if he were around more.
paragraphs.translationZh: (8) 这种变化不仅对女性有利，尤其对男性和儿童也有利。刻板的五点钟爸爸属于一幅画，他的“问你妈妈”和他的“不要成为一个爱哭鬼”。认为拥抱和亲吻是性别盲目以及脏尿布需要更换的父亲无疑是更可取的。如果他能多在身边该多高兴啊。

paragraphs.sourceText: (9) “This is the man’s half of having it all,” said Donald Long, a professor who teaches a course about men’s relationships that drew 135 students this year for thirty-five places, “We’re trying to do what women want of us, what children want of us, but we’re not willing to transform the workplace.” In other words, the hearts and minds of today’s fathers are definitely in the right place, if only their bodies could be there, too.
paragraphs.translationZh: (9) “这是男人拥有一切的一半，”教授唐纳德·朗 (Donald Long) 说，他教授一门有关男性关系的课程，今年吸引了 135 名学生参加了 35 个名额，“我们正在努力做女性想要我们做的事情，孩子们想要我们做的事情，但我们不愿意改变工作场所。”换句话说，今天的父亲们的心灵和思想肯定是在正确的地方，只要他们的身体也能在那里就好了。

paragraphs.sourceText: (1) When a Southerner took the trouble to pack a trunk and travel twenty miles for a visit, the visit was seldom of shorter duration than a month, usually much longer. Southerners were as enthusiastic visitors as they were hosts, and there was nothing unusual in relatives coming to spend the Christmas holidays and remaining until July. Often when newly married couples went on the usual round of honeymoon visits, they lingered in some pleasant home until the birth of their second child. Frequently elderly aunts and uncles came to Sunday dinner and remained until they were buried years later. Visitors presented no problem, for houses were larger, servants numerous and the feeding of several extra mouths a minor matter in that land of plenty. All ages and sexes went visiting, honeymooners, young mothers showing off new babies, convalescents, the bereaved, girls whose parents were anxious to remove them from the dangers of unwise matches, girls who had reached the danger age without becoming engaged and who, it was hoped, would make suitable matches under the guidance of relatives in other places. Visitors added excitement and variety to the slow-moving Southern life and they were always welcome.
paragraphs.translationZh: (1) 当一个南方人不厌其烦地收拾行李，长途跋涉二十英里去拜访时，访问的时间很少会短于一个月，通常会更长。南方人既是热情的主人，也是热情的访客，亲戚们来过圣诞假期并一直待到七月，这并没有什么不寻常的。通常，当新婚夫妇去度蜜月时，他们会在一些舒适的家里逗留，直到他们的第二个孩子出生。年老的阿姨和叔叔经常来参加周日的晚餐，并留下来直到几年后被埋葬。来访者没有任何问题，因为房子更大，仆人众多，在这片富饶的土地上，多吃几张嘴只是小事。各个年龄段和性别的人都来拜访，有度蜜月的新婚夫妇、炫耀新生婴儿的年轻母亲、康复者、失去亲人的人、父母急于将她们从不明智婚姻中解救出来的女孩、已经到了订婚危险年龄但希望能在其他地方的亲戚指导下进行合适婚姻的女孩。游客们为缓慢发展的南方生活增添了刺激和多样性，他们总是受到欢迎。

paragraphs.sourceText: (2) So Scarlett had come to Atlanta with no idea as to how long she would remain. If her visit proved as dull as those in Savannah and Charleston, she would return home in a month. If her stay was pleasant, she would remain indefinitely. But no sooner had she arrived than Aunt Pitty and Melanie began a campaign to induce her to make her home permanently with them. They brought up every possible argument. They wanted her for her own self because they loved her. They were lonely and often frightened at night in the big house, and she was so brave she gave them courage. She was so charming that she cheered them in their sorrow. Now that Charles was dead, her place and her son’s place were with his kindred. Besides, half the house now belonged to her, through Charles’ will. Last, the Confederacy needed every pair of hands for sewing, knitting, bandage rolling and nursing the wounded.
paragraphs.translationZh: (2) 斯嘉丽来到亚特兰大时并不知道自己会待多久。如果她的访问像萨凡纳和查尔斯顿那样乏味，她将在一个月后回家。如果她的逗留愉快，她将无限期地留下来。但她一到，皮蒂姨妈和梅兰妮就开始了一场活动，诱使她和她们一起永久定居。他们提出了所有可能的论据。他们想要她自己，因为他们爱她。他们在大房子里感到孤独，晚上常常感到害怕，而她很勇敢，给了他们勇气。她是如此迷人，以至于在他们的悲伤中为他们欢呼。现在查尔斯死了，她和她儿子的位置都和他的亲属在一起了。此外，根据查尔斯的遗嘱，一半的房子现在属于她。最后，联邦需要每一双手来缝纫、编织、卷绷带和护理伤员。

paragraphs.sourceText: (3) Charles’ Uncle Henry Hamilton, who lived in bachelor state at the Atlanta Hotel near the depot, also talked seriously to her on this subject. Uncle Henry was a short, pot-bellied, irascible old gentleman with a pink face, a shock of long silver hair and an utter lack of patience with feminine timidities and vaporings. It was for the latter reason that he was barely on speaking terms with his sister, Miss Pitty. From childhood, they had been exact opposites in temperament and they had been further estranged by his objections to the manner in which she had reared Charles “Making a damn sissy out of a soldier’s son!” Years before, he had so insulted her that now Miss Pitty never spoke of him except in guarded whispers and with so great reticence that a stranger would have thought the honest old lawyer a murderer, at the least. The insult had occurred on a day when Pitty wished to draw five hundred dollars from her estate, of which he was trustee, to invest in a non-existent gold mine. He had refused to permit it and stated heatedly that she had no more sense than a June bug and furthermore it gave him the fidgets to be around her longer than five minutes. Since that day, she only saw him formally, once a month, when Uncle Peter drove her to his office to get the housekeeping money. After these brief visits, Pitty always took to her bed for the rest of the day with tears and smelling salts. Melanie and Charles, who were on excellent terms with their uncle, had frequently offered to relieve her of this ordeal, but Pitty always set her babyish mouth firmly and refused. Henry was her cross and she must bear him. From this, Charles and Melanie could only infer that she took a profound pleasure in this occasional excitement, the only excitement in her sheltered life.
paragraphs.translationZh: （3）查尔斯的舅舅亨利·汉密尔顿，住在车站附近的亚特兰大酒店，住在单身状态，也认真地和她谈论过这个话题。亨利叔叔是一位身材矮小、大腹便便、脾气暴躁的老绅士，粉红色的脸庞，一头蓬乱的银色长发，对女性的胆怯和情绪完全缺乏耐心。正是由于后一个原因，他才和他的妹妹皮蒂小姐很少说话。从孩提时代起，他们的性情就截然相反，而且他反对她抚养查尔斯的方式，“把一个士兵的儿子变成了一个该死的娘娘腔！”，这进一步疏远了他们。几年前，他曾如此侮辱过她，以至于现在皮蒂小姐从来不谈起他，除非是小心翼翼地低声交谈，而且非常沉默寡言，以至于陌生人至少会认为这位诚实的老律师是杀人犯。这次侮辱发生的一天，皮蒂希望从她的遗产中提取五百美元（他是该遗产的受托人）来投资一个不存在的金矿。他拒绝允许，并激烈地声称她的理智不比六月虫子强，而且在她身边超过五分钟让他坐立不安。从那天起，她只正式见到他，每月一次，当时彼得叔叔开车送她去他的办公室拿家务费。在这些短暂的拜访之后，皮蒂总是在一天剩下的时间里躺在床上，流着泪，闻着盐味。梅兰妮和查尔斯与叔叔关系很好，经常主动提出要帮她摆脱这种痛苦，但皮蒂总是坚定她幼稚的嘴，拒绝了。亨利是她的十字架，她必须忍受他。由此，查尔斯和梅兰妮只能推断，她对这种偶尔的兴奋感到深深的快乐，这是她受庇护的生活中唯一的兴奋。

paragraphs.sourceText: (4) Uncle Henry liked Scarlett immediately because, he said, he could see that for all her silly affectations she had a few grains of sense. He was trustee, not only of Pitty’s and Melanie’s estates, but also of that left Scarlett by Charles.
paragraphs.translationZh: (4) 亨利叔叔立刻就喜欢上了斯嘉丽，因为他说，他可以看出，尽管她有些愚蠢的矫揉造作，但她还是有一点理智的。他不仅是皮蒂和梅兰妮遗产的受托人，也是查尔斯留给斯嘉丽遗产的受托人。

paragraphs.sourceText: Two indigenous languages are dying out every month
paragraphs.translationZh: 两种土著语言每个月都在消失

paragraphs.sourceText: Despite UN efforts to highlight the daily disappearance of mother tongues across the world, the President of the General Assembly (PGA) warned that “challenges persist nonetheless”. “Every fortnight, at least one indigenous language vanishes from the face of the earth,” spelled out the PGA. “This translates into two extinct indigenous languages each month.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管联合国努力强调世界各地母语每天都在消失，但大会主席（PGA）警告说，“挑战仍然存在”。 PGA 指出：“每两周，至少有一种土著语言从地球表面消失。” “这每个月都会翻译成两种已灭绝的土著语言。”

paragraphs.sourceText: He said it was “equally noteworthy,” that 15 per cent of the poorest people on the planet are indigenous.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他说，“同样值得注意”的是，地球上 15% 的最贫困人口是土著。

paragraphs.sourceText: Indigenous traditions have served as a “dependable means of acquiring knowledge” which can be transmitted across generations, he stated, citing examples of herbal medicine, food processing and settling disputes within communities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他引用草药、食品加工和解决社区内争端的例子表示，土著传统是“获取知识的可靠手段”，可以代代相传。

paragraphs.sourceText: And although linguistic diversity is essential to preserve humanity’s common heritage, which is critical to its survival, it is endangered with every language that goes extinct.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管语言多样性对于保护人类的共同遗产至关重要，而这对人类的生存至关重要，但随着每一种语言的灭绝，语言多样性都受到了威胁。

paragraphs.sourceText: “With the death of languages, the indigenous people who speak them lose a significant part of their identity,” he lamented.
paragraphs.translationZh: “随着语言的消亡，使用这些语言的土著人民失去了他们身份的重要部分，”他感叹道。

paragraphs.sourceText: He urged the world to focus attention on the measures to ensure the survival of those which remain, underscoring that “schools have a major role to play”.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他敦促世界关注确保留下来的人生存的措施，并强调“学校可以发挥重要作用”。

paragraphs.sourceText: “By integrating indigenous languages into their curricula, they would have fulfilled the vital mission of shielding the languages from external damage and internal decline,” said the PGA.
paragraphs.translationZh: PGA 表示：“通过将土著语言纳入课程，他们本可以完成保护语言免受外部损害和内部衰落的重要使命。”

options.reflowSourceText: Visitors tended to stay much longer than planned.
options.translationZh: 游客停留的时间往往比计划的要长得多。

options.sourceText: Visitors were usually young and married couples.
options.reflowSourceText: Visitors were usually young and married couples.
options.translationZh: 来访者通常是年轻的和已婚的夫妇。

options.sourceText: Southerners liked to show hospitality to their guests.
options.reflowSourceText: Southerners liked to show hospitality to their guests.

options.sourceText: Southerners were wealthy enough to receive guests.
options.reflowSourceText: Southerners were wealthy enough to receive guests.
options.translationZh: 南方人有钱，可以接待客人。
